problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & -1 \\ 4 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors ${i,j,k}$ of ${R}^{3}$ under the action of $T?$

activity_context.topic_title: The Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation in Terms of the Standard Basis

feedback.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ has the standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

 
What are the respective images of the standard basis vectors ${i,j}$ of ${R}^{2}$ under the action of $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The images of the vectors in the standard basis ${i,j}$ are the first and second columns of $T,$ respectively. 

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

We can find the images of the vectors in the standard basis ${i,j}$ by computing the matrix products $T\cdot i$ and $T\cdot j:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(i) & =T\cdot i=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T(j) & =T\cdot j=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
